findings.evidence: `roadmap/.../Suggested.lean:163` declares `centralizer_isSimpleRing`; grep finds only `Centralizer.lean:227: theorem isSimpleRing_centralizer`.
findings.fix: Rename the theorem or add `centralizer_isSimpleRing` as the canonical alias.
findings.issue: The roadmap target is named `centralizer_isSimpleRing`, but the PR exports only `isSimpleRing_centralizer`, breaking the pinned public API.

findings.evidence: Lines 61–130 expose `Bimodule`, `of`, `toEnd`, and the module instances; all external grep hits in Skolem–Noether and Centralizer use named interface lemmas rather than requiring body reduction.
findings.fix: Remove the section-wide `@[expose]`; keep definitions opaque and prove interface equations inside this module (using `:= (rfl)` where appropriate).
findings.issue: `@[expose] public section` exposes every implementation body in the bimodule construction, although consumers use the provided `smul_def`, `smul_of`, and `symm_smul` interface.

findings.evidence: Lines 107, 136, and 208 carry `@[expose]`; lines 108–212 are used only to build `centralizerAlgEquivEnd`, and grep finds no `centralizerAlgEquivEnd ... .symm` characterization.
findings.fix: Make the construction helpers private, remove `@[expose]` from the equivalence, retain the forward simp lemma, and add a simp lemma identifying `(centralizerAlgEquivEnd B).symm φ` with evaluation of `φ` at `1`.
findings.issue: The equivalence construction leaks `centralizerMulLeftEnd`, `centralizerAlgHom`, its bijectivity proof, and exposed bodies, while its API only characterizes the forward map and not the inverse.

summary: The public surface exposes implementation bodies and scaffolding while omitting the roadmap-compatible theorem name and a characteristic inverse lemma.
